items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: Benny Carter discusses a songwriting credit dispute involving Sammy Cahn and Nicholas Bronsky, but does not describe a personal or professional relationship with Sammy Cahn himself.

ctx.x: was that Sammy Cahn has, inadvertently, of course, written, or used the same title that he had used for another song, with which, you know, that he had collaborated with Nicholas Bronsky on. And I don't know how labeling or programming or whoever the people at the record company could have gotten his name on it, because they would certainly have received the music, you know, from my own song. I would think so -- or maybe they just took the title and just looked it up in the ASCAP files or something and said,…

But Sammy had forgotten that he had written another song by this title. Noe he's a very prolific writer, as we know -- but the funny thing about it was I dismissed it then; I said, "Well, it's probably some little insignificant song that they wrote" -- and never did anything with more.

And then just a few months ago, I was looking at late television and I don't know why I happened to look at a picture called "Ten Thousand Bedrooms" with Dean Martin -- and here's this song, "Only Trust Your Heart". But of course, it's the Nicholas Bronsky melody, and the other Sammy Cahn lyric. But the only thing that's the same about our song is the title.
